brief:
A new assessment has found a sharp rise in cases where children are deliberately denied humanitarian assistance in conflict zones, The Guardian reported. The analysis identified a pattern of "weaponisation" of aid becoming normalised in active conflicts, with the majority of documented incidents occurring in Palestine.

The deliberate restrictions on aid delivery have left children facing acute shortages of food, water, and medical care in active fighting zones, transforming humanitarian access into a contested battlefield tactic rather than a civilian protection.
